questions.q: What did Databricks & Delta Lake Lessons 48-57 already cover, according to this lesson?
options: Lakeflow as the unified name for ingestion, pipelines, and orchestration, plus the Delta Live Tables rename
The SQL syntax for CREATE STREAMING TABLE
Job cluster vs. all-purpose cluster cost differences
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly builds on Lesson 48's coverage of Lakeflow and the DLT rename rather than re-teaching it.

questions.q: What is the current, recommended Python import for writing Lakeflow pipeline code, according to this lesson?
options: from pyspark import pipelines as dp
questions.explain: The dlt module still works but is now the legacy path; pyspark.pipelines (imported as dp) is current and recommended.

questions.q: What is the open-source engine that Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines runs on and extends?
questions.explain: Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines is built on the open-source Apache Spark Declarative Pipelines engine, available since Spark 4.1.

questions.q: What comparison does this chapter draw, as distinct from Lesson 56's Lakeflow-vs-ADF comparison?
options: Lakeflow's declarative pipelines against the manual bronze-to-silver-to-gold pipeline this track built by hand
questions.explain: Lesson 56 already compared Lakeflow to ADF; this chapter compares it to this track's own manual medallion pipeline from Lessons 25-37.

questions.q: In the manual medallion pipeline from Lessons 25-37, how was execution order determined?
options: Wired by hand — tasks were chained together explicitly, as in Lesson 30
Determined by the cluster's available memory
There was no execution order — everything ran simultaneously
questions.explain: The manual pipeline required the author to explicitly chain tasks in order, unlike a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline's inferred dependency graph.
